Group Risk Management Policy GRP-POL-001 | Version 6.0 | Internal

3. Regulatory context and standards alignment

The framework is designed to satisfy the supervisory expectations of the Group's principal regulators while remaining a single, internally coherent framework rather than a collection of jurisdiction-specific approaches.

3.1 External standards

STANDARD OR FRAMEWORK RELEVANCE TO THIS POLICY HOW ALIGNMENT IS ACHIEVED

ISO 31000:2018 — Risk Provides the process model and vocabulary Section 10 mirrors the ISO process; Section 4 adopts ISOmanagement guidelines consistent definitions

COSO Enterprise Risk Management _ Integrates risk with strategy and performance Appetite is set alongside the strategic plan (Section 8.2) (2017)

Basel — Sound Management of Operational risk governance, three lines, loss Sections 6, 13 and 16 Operational Risk data BCBS 239 — Risk Data Aggregation Accuracy, completeness and timeliness of risk Section 19.4 data quality requirements data

IIA Three Lines Model (2020) Accountability and assurance structure Section 6 ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and NIST CSF _ Technology and cyber risk control objectives Technology & Cyber Risk Policy (GRP-POL-014) 2.0

NIST SP 800-37 Risk Management System-level risk authorisation Change and system approval process, Section 18.1 Framework

PRA Operational Resilience Important business services and impact Section 17.4 (SS1/21) tolerances EU Digital Operational Resilience Act ICT risk and third-party oversight in the EU Sections 18.3 and 17.4 (DORA) GDPR, UK DPA 2018, DPDP Act Personal data as a risk category Data Privacy Policy (GRP-POL-021); taxonomy Level 2 "Data 2023, GLBA privacy”

3.2 Regulatory relationship awn

Each principal supervisory relationship has a single named owner accountable for the accuracy and timeliness of submissions and for coordinating examination responses.

REGULATOR RELATIONSHIP OWNER CONTACT DEPUTY

Federal Reserve / OCC Yevgeni A. Sorokina, Group y.sorokina@cadencefg.com, +1 (212) Marta Szewczyk (+48 22 555 0164) CFO 555-0121

PRA/ FCA Desmond N. Quarshie d.quarshie@cadencefg.com, +44 20 Tobias Lindqvist 7555 0129

AMF (France) Mireille Dubois-Kane m.duboiskane@cadencefg.com, +33 1 Helena Vorstermann 5555 0144

RBI (India) Devansh R. Kulkarni d.kulkarni@cadencefg.com, +91 80 Ananya V. Chatterjee 4555 0182

MAS (Singapore) Aiko Nakamura-Reed a.nakamurareed@cadencefg.com, Hiroshi Yamagata

+65 6555 0172

Data protection authorities Helena Vorstermann, CPO h.vorstermann@cadencefg.com, +44 ‘Tobias Lindqvist 20 7555 0163

3.3 Relationship to the internal control framework

Risk assessment determines what could go wrong and how severely; the control framework determines what is done to prevent or detect it. The two are linked through the control library, in which every control maps to at least one risk in the Group Risk Register, and every risk rated Elevated or above maps to at least one control.

3.4 Relationship to capital and liquidity planning

The output of risk identification and assessment is a direct input to the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP) and the Internal Liquidity Adequacy Assessment Process (ILAAP). Material risks not adequately captured by regulatory capital requirements are assessed for Pillar 2 add-ons by the Group Treasurer, Marta Szewczyk (m.szewczyk@cadencefg.com), with challenge from the Group Chief Risk Officer.

3.5 Cross-border considerations

Each regulated subsidiary maintains a board-approved local addendum documenting the local regulatory overlay, the composition of the local risk committee and the delegated authorities of local management. Local addenda may narrow Group appetite but may never widen it. Cross-border data flows arising from Group-level risk aggregation — which include the employee identifiers and contact details reproduced throughout this policy — are assessed under the Data Privacy Policy before transfer.
